evidence.source: Adam Khoo — Will Rising Long Term Rates Crash Stocks? (Sep 14)
evidence.claim: Long rate ≈ inflation + real GDP: 3.4% CPI + 1.5% GDP = 4.9% and heading toward 5–5.5%; the Fed controls only the short rate — a hot-inflation regime mechanically pushes long yields up regardless of Fed policy
evidence.relation: inflation-anchored long-rate drift up → 20+yr bond prices down

resolution: Consistent with the bearish market prior (hot-CPI buckets + hike odds pressuring the long end); Khoo's mechanism reinforces it. His counterpoint — 5% yields are historically normal and only a fast spike hurts — is equity-focused and does not protect 20+yr bond prices from a further yield grind higher.
